Deion Sanders has opened up on the brutal rule he enforces for people staying over at his house

Deion Sanders has hilariously revealed that he maintains a "three-day rule" for people staying in his house, and that not even his family is exempt.

The Colorado Buffaloes head coach has been making the most of his offseason by making regular appearances on his popular talk show, "We Got Time Today", alongside co-host Rocsi Diaz, and a clip from a recent episode has gone viral after Sanders opened up on his life behind closed doors.

It comes in the same week that "Coach Prime" doubled down on his claims that he would never coach in the NFL, despite previous rumors linking him to the Dallas Cowboys vacancy, and that he had previously admitted coaching at the professional level is unlikely for him.

This week, Sanders found himself doing the rounds on social media once more when a clip of him revealing his "three-day rule" went viral, during which he offered an incredible example as to why nobody should expect to stay any longer in his house.

"I have a three-day rule in my house," Sanders began in an episode of "We Got Time Today". "If Jesus got up on the third day, you're going to. I'm not letting nobody, family included - you're not staying at my house over three days."

His revelation left Diaz and special guests, former NBA players Matt Barnes and Stephen Jackson, in fits of laughter, but Sanders wasn't done there; he then laid out the blueprint for visiting him.

"First day, we cool, we kick it," Sanders continued. "The second day, I'm going to take you somewhere, what you want to do? Third day, I'm looking at you like, 'All right now though, come on now.'"

The 58-year-old's comments soon brought smiles to the faces of those watching on social media, with many quick to share their thoughts on his unusual yet arguably fair stance on having visitors in his house.

"Coach Prime doesn't care if you're family or a friend. After Day 3 of staying under his roof, it's time to make other arrangements," one person laughed on X. "It really be like that," joked another.

A third person wrote, "I totally agree with him. That's why when I go home, I stay at a hotel," while a fourth added, "You shouldn't stay longer than fish in the refrigerator. That's a solid principle to go by."

Not even Sanders' family, including his son, Shedeur (pictured), is safe from his 'three-day rule'(Image: AP)

Sanders is currently gearing up for his seventh season as a college football head coach and fourth in charge of Colorado in 2026, though he is arguably under the most pressure he has ever faced during his Buffaloes tenure.

Following a difficult 3-9 (1-8 Big 12) campaign in 2025, taking his overall record with Colorado to 16-21 (9-18), many believe that Sanders is facing a defining, make-or-break fourth year with the Buffaloes in 2026.

Major media outlets such as CBS Sports have already dropped him to No. 60 overall in their Power Four coach rankings, though putting together a top 25 transfer class this offseason may well be his saving grace.
